title: {name} bot protection: how to detect it (and what it means for scraping)
intro: {name} is a bot protection or anti-abuse layer that some websites put in front of their pages. If you are looking for a {name} bypass, trying to detect {name} on a site, or investigating web scraping blocked by {name}, the first step is the same: confirm that {name} is really what answers your requests. This page lists the {total} public signals that the Scrapfly Antibot Detector extension uses to recognise {name} bot detection, how strongly each one points to it, and what that usually means for an automated client.
headingHow: How to tell a site uses {name}
howIntro: These signals are generated from the extension's own detection rules for `{id}` (rule version {version}, last updated {updated}). A signal is only an indication: confidence is how sure the extension is when that one signal is seen. Signals marked "corroboration only" never count on their own, because other products can produce them too.
sectionCookieIntro: Cookie names (and values, where one is matched) set on the page. Patterns are regular expressions unless they are plain words.
sectionHeaderIntro: HTTP response headers the page or its requests return.
sectionUrlIntro: Addresses of scripts, frames and requests the page loads. These are patterns matched against the full address.
sectionContentIntro: Text found inside the page or its scripts.
sectionWindowIntro: Properties the page's own JavaScript context exposes on `window`.
sectionPayloadIntro: Data the page sends to, or receives from, a matching address.
combinationsIntro: Some signals score higher together than alone. These combinations are what the extension also reports.
difficultyTextLow: Low means the extension rates this protection as a light obstacle: it usually only filters simple clients, and a real browser or a well-formed browser-like request often gets through.
difficultyTextMedium: Medium means the extension rates this protection as a real obstacle: expect checks on the browser, on request details, or on both, and expect them to change over time.
difficultyTextHigh: High means the extension rates this protection as among the hardest to get past: it typically combines client-side checks with behavioural or server-side scoring.
difficultyNote: The rating is the extension's own rule of thumb, not a statement by the vendor, and a site's configuration can make the same product easier or harder.
scrapingMeaning: If {name} is present, a request that does not look like a real, consistent browser session may be challenged, delayed or refused, and the response can be a challenge or block page instead of the content you wanted. What exactly happens depends on how the site owner configured the product, which can differ from one site to the next and can change without notice. Treat a detection as a reason to look at the response you actually receive, not as a guarantee of a block.
scrapingScrapfly: To scrape pages protected by {name} without maintaining the workarounds yourself, see Scrapfly's {aspLink} and the {apiLink}. Only scrape what you are allowed to, and respect the site's terms and robots rules.
detectText: Install the free {storeLink} for Chrome, browse to the page, and the popup lists {name} with its confidence, its difficulty and the exact signals that matched. Read more in the {readmeLink}, or see {allLink}.
linkAll: all anti-bot protections the extension detects
indexTitle: Anti-bot protections the Antibot Detector recognises
indexIntro: One page for each of the {count} anti-bot detectors in the {extLink} extension: what the protection is, the public signals that reveal it, how hard it is rated, and what it usually means for web scraping. Pages are generated from the detection rules in `detectors/antibot/`. To get past anti-bot systems at scale, see Scrapfly's {aspLink}.
